newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants concrete steps on Serbian elections.
newsitem.headline: France wants concrete steps on Serbian elections.

text.p: France, preparing for a visit by leaders of Serbia's Zajedno democratic opposition coalition, urged Belgrade on Wednesday to take concrete steps toward recognising opposition victories in November's local polls.

Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, in a concession to pro-democracy demonstrators, announced on Tuesday he wanted parliament to approve special legislation reinstating the disputed results of elections in 14 cities and towns including Belgrade itself.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said he hoped the move was not simply a delaying tactic.
In a statement read to reporters by Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt, de Charette said Milosevic's announcement "appears to be a step in the right direction.

"I hope this is not a delaying tactic attempting to shift responsibility for the law's rejection to the parliament. If, on the other hand, this announcement is followed by concrete steps, France will be the first to offer its congratulations," de Charette said in the statement.
Stepping up the pressure, France said on Monday it was recognising the opposition coalition by inviting its leaders to Paris for talks.

Paris said that opposition leaders Zoran Djindjic, Vuk Draskovic and Vesna Pesic had proved their "political maturity" and added it hoped its invitation would help promote a dialogue between them and the hardline Socialist president.
